newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian TV says Chechen bosses in hostage-machine.
newsitem.headline: Russian TV says Chechen bosses in hostage-machine.

text.p: The head of Russia's NTV commercial television channel on Tuesday accused the leaders of Chechnya of being involved in the capture of three of his journalists and other hostages in the rebel republic.

Igor Malashenko told a news conference his company had been forced to pay a ransom for the release of the three, who returned to Moscow on Monday after 100 days in captivity, much of which they said they had spent in a mountain cave.
He refused to name the exact sum but said it was seven digits in dollars.

"All this is a big hostage-taking machine...under the direct leadership of Vice President Vakha Arsanov. Today we have no doubts about this," said Mal, seated alongside one of the three, award-winning correspondent Yelena Masyuk.

"We are sure that President (Aslan) Maskhadov, who visited Moscow yesterday, is at the very least aware of what is going on in his republic and...is either too weak and cannot help to free people or can and doesn't want to," he added.

Malashenko said he did not know whether President Boris Yeltsin, who hosted Maskhadov in the Kremlin on Monday for talks on relations between Russia and its breakaway republic, knew what was going on but urged him to take measures to stop it.
"The Russian state...turned out to be unable to protect its citizens and unable to free its citizens on the territory of the Russian Federation," he said.
Officials in Chechnya could not immediately be contacted for comment.
